paper_title: Learning Active Subspaces and Discovering Interpretability in Neural Networks
core_problem: The conflicting nature of achieving strong predictive performance and human interpretability in machine learning models.
methodology_summary: A modification of the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) where the Gaussian kernel is equipped with a learnable precision matrix. The eigenvectors of this matrix reveal the active subspace and allow for ranking input variable importance.
datasets_eval: Not specified, but experiments were conducted for regression, classification, and feature selection tasks.
empirical_results: The proposed model achieved attractive prediction performance compared to popular ML models, state-of-the-art deep learning embedding techniques, and a transformer model, while also providing meaningful interpretability.
explicit_limitations: Standard Gaussian kernels often assume an isotropic covariance (equal variance across features), treating all features equally, whereas the proposed method allows for learning a full precision matrix to capture distinct variances.
